title: Procurement workspace manifest
description: Identity card for one procurement workspace, written to procurement.json at the workspace root. Present whether the workspace is a standalone repo or a folder inside a parent repo, so that a single scan over a tree can enumerate every procurement exercise regardless of how it was provisioned. This file is the join key for any later index or database: the id never changes once written.

schema_version.description: Version of this manifest format. Bumped when the shape changes, so an index can read old workspaces.

id.description: Stable workspace id, PW-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX. Date is the opening date; the suffix is random hex. Sortable, greppable, typable, and never reused or rewritten — renaming the directory does not change it.

name.description: Kebab-case slug. Matches the directory name at creation time but is not required to stay in sync if the directory is later renamed.

title.description: One line, human-facing: what is actually being bought or surveyed.

variant.description: Which scaffold this workspace was created from. Determines which commands apply.

mode.description: repo: standalone git repository, provisioned by new-workspace. folder: a directory inside a parent repo, provisioned by workspace-folder.

visibility.description: Intended visibility. Private is the default for every variant; a procurement workspace states what someone is planning to buy and what they will pay.

status.description: Lifecycle. open: research in progress. decided: a recommendation exists but nothing bought. purchased: closed by a purchase. abandoned: closed without one. superseded: replaced by another workspace, named in supersedes/superseded_by.

opened.description: ISO date the workspace was provisioned. Absolute, never relative.

updated.description: ISO date of the last manifest write.

closed.description: ISO date the status moved to purchased, abandoned or superseded. Null while open or decided.

parent.description: Set for mode=folder. Identifies the repo this folder lives inside, so an index can group siblings.

repo.description: Parent repo name or remote URL.

path.description: Path of this folder relative to the parent repo root.

spec.description: Pointer to the governing spec artefact, so a report can state which revision it judged against.

path.description: Relative path, e.g. spec.yaml or spec.md.

revision.description: Mirrors spec.yaml revision. Absent for prose-only specs.

variants.description: Sibling variant spec paths when spec-variants is in use, e.g. spec-budget.yaml.

reports.description: Every dated report ever produced, appended and never rewritten. This is the audit trail — a report that is not listed here is not discoverable by an index.

path.description: Relative path to the markdown twin, which always exists.

pdf.description: Relative path to the compiled PDF, null if Typst was unavailable or --md-only was passed.

spec_revision.description: Spec revision the report judged against. Lets a reader tell a stale report from a current one.

candidates.description: How many candidates the report covered.

headline.description: One line: the pick, or the finding that nothing qualified.

outcome.description: What was actually bought. Written when status moves to purchased. The point of recording it is that it can be compared against the spec later.

matched_report.description: Path of the report whose recommendation was followed, or null if the purchase departed from it.

tags.description: Free-form kebab-case labels for grouping across workspaces, e.g. home-lab, audio, tooling.

generator.description: What wrote this workspace, for reproducibility.

scaffold.description: Where the scaffold came from: bundled, or a template repo reference.
